The '''Cold Big Bang''' hypothesis is an attempt to explain the origin of the [[Universe]].

== The early Universe according to Cold Big Bang ==

[[File:Cold-Big-Bang-Early-Universe-Sequence.svg|center]]

== Problems with the Cold Bang Hypothesis ==

Four independent groups of scientists investigated the Cold Bang hypothesis between the 1940s and the 1960s:

* Gamow (1940s)
* Zel’dovitch (1964)
* Hoyle and Tayler (1964)
* Peebles (1965) 

Similar negative conclusions were reached:

* Nucleosynthesis in a dense nucleon–electron gas predicts hydrogen formation to be strongly suppressed relative to heavier elements, and
* this prediction contradicts a large primordial hydrogen abundance observed in our Universe.

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

== Subsequent proposals ==

The [[Hot Big Bang Model]], in which the early Universe was dominated by radiation instead of matter, was proposed to replace the Cold Big Bang model.<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
